verses.1: So, he had the first rights of worship, along with the sacred religious objects.
verses.2: For the first stage was built in the same place where the table and the dishes were placed. This is what’s called “Hagia”.
verses.3: After the second fall, there is a scene called “Hagia Hagiōn”.
verses.4: It had a golden altar and the box containing the treasures, all covered with gold. In this golden altar were also the staff and the rod of Aaron, as well as the decorations that adorned the box.
verses.5: Above her, however, the glory of Heruviel shines brightly; it’s impossible to describe in detail what that means now.
verses.6: And with these being arranged in this manner, in the first scene, the priests carried out their rituals by entering there.
verses.7: But in the second day of the year, only the high priest could do this. It wasn’t just blood that was offered; he also offered sacrifices for himself and for the people.
verses.8: By saying this about the spirit of the saint, it means that the path of the saints cannot be revealed yet, at the moment when we first enter that stage.
verses.9: It’s a metaphor for the time that has come. In this time, both gifts and sacrifices cannot be offered in a way that truly honors those who are worshipped.
verses.10: Only through rituals, offerings, and various baptisms can the rights of the flesh be restored to their proper state.
verses.11: But Christ, who became an archangel of all the good deeds that have been done, did not touch them with His hands. This is not the way in which this building was constructed.
verses.12: Neither through the blood of animals nor through the blood of thieves; rather, through one’s own blood, he entered into holiness, finding eternal redemption.
verses.13: For indeed, the blood of animals and birds, along with the dust from the earth, purifies those who are involved in such acts, making them pure in relation to their physical bodies.
verses.14: How much more precious is the blood of Christ, who, through the Spirit of eternity, united himself alone to God. He cleanses our consciousness from all dead works, so that we may worship God while still alive.
verses.15: And because of this new covenant, those who are entitled to inherit from the original covenant will no longer be able to die and then be freed from their obligations under that covenant.
verses.16: For where there is a contract, one must bear the death penalty for what has been contracted.
verses.17: For the testament is indeed valid for the deceased, as long as the person who makes it is still alive.
verses.18: Nor is the first place any longer clear from bloodstains.
verses.19: For according to the law given by Moses, it was necessary for all people to obey his commands. He took the blood of the priests along with water, as well as the incense and the other offerings. Then he wrote down everything in that book, and everyone was required to follow those instructions.
verses.20: “This is the blood of the covenant that God has set between us.”
verses.21: And he also allocated the stage and all the equipment necessary for the performance to those who were responsible for carrying out the task.
verses.22: And almost everything is cleaned up according to the law. Without any need for bloodletting, there is no need for destruction.
verses.23: Therefore, it is necessary to purify those examples that are found in the heavens. Meanwhile, those airy substances must be sacrificed to them.
verses.24: For the holy Christ did not enter into human form, as it were in a physical body. Instead, he entered into the heavens themselves. Now, his face appears before us, as if He were God himself.
verses.25: Nor should he offer himself too often, just as the high priest enters the holy places once a year, in another state of impurity.
verses.26: Since he had to suffer many times due to the suffering of this world, now, at the end of time, he is revealed in order to atone for his sins through his sacrifice.
verses.27: And as far as it concerns human beings, the ultimate death is inevitable. After that, however, there’s still a decision to be made.
verses.28: In the same way, Christ, who always refused to accept sin from many people, will also accept sin from those who accept Him as their Savior.
